why: THE WRITER-SIDE TWIN OF `PROP_CALLBACK`.
A terminal writer whose only caller is a shared executor that RECEIVES it as
an injected port has a real call edge and runs in production — but the call
site is `port.method(...)` on a parameter, and no static resolution can
follow that. Left alone the analyzer reports it as DEAD_UNREACHABLE, which
is the one thing it definitely is not.
The alternatives were considered and are worse. Removing the injection would
mean either duplicating the executor per host — the exact duplication the
Evidence Lifecycle Convergence existed to remove, since two of the four
destroyers it replaced certified destructions they never performed — or
building a third S3 client inside the shared package, re-implementing the TLS
and endpoint safety rules that each host already applies to its own. A third
construction of the rules that decide whether a delete may leave the machine
is not an improvement on an analyzer blind spot.
So each injected implementation is read ONCE and recorded here with the four
links of its chain. The generator RE-VERIFIES all four on every run:
- `adapter` must exist and must reference the writer's declaration;
- `executor` must exist and must call the port method;
- `entrypoints` must each exist and must reference the executor;
- the writer itself must still exist at the declaration named.
Any link that breaks fails the run rather than leaving a stale exemption. An
entry that matches no writer is reported for the same reason: a manifest that
silently stops describing the tree is worse than no manifest.
These land in the PORT_ATTRIBUTED_REACHABLE bucket, counted separately and
never folded into the route- or job-attributed totals. 'Reached only through
injection' is a weaker claim than 'reached by a route' and reads as one.

implementations.evidence: The ONE physical evidence-destruction executor deletes storage objects through the injected port. The API host supplies `apiEvidenceDestructionStorage`, whose `deleteObject` IS this function by direct reference. Both entrypoints are route-driven: `executeDestruction` (POST /v1/product-and-lifecycle destruction execute) and `executeApprovedReview` (destruction-review execute). Exercised end to end against a disposable object store by services/api/test/evidence-destruction-storage.integration.test.ts, which drives the real executor through the real port shape.

The worker half of the same one executor. `workerEvidenceDestructionStorage.deleteObject` wraps this function to normalise its throw-on-failure into the port's result shape (the API's already returns a result). Both entrypoints are queue- or sweep-driven: `processPurgeDeletedEvidence` (PurgeDeletedEvidenceJob) and `runDestructionOrchestration` (DestructionOrchestratorSweep). Before the convergence this function was reached directly from the purge job's own inline storage loop; the loop is gone because the purge job no longer decides or performs destruction.
